title: 5 Strikers Man Utd Could Sign in January After Benjamin Sesko Blow
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTMan Utd must analyze short-term solutions to their No. 9 problem. / Sebastian Frej (Mateta), Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Endrick)Respite has been in short supply for Manchester United this season.

On-field performances have been disastrous, players have publicly lambasted club staff and, just to make matters even worse, injuries have poured fuel on a growing dumpster fire. When it rains, it pours—as those familiar with the Manchester climate know all too well.

The latest setback amid the ongoing crisis comes from the treatment room, as Benjamin Šeško’s return from a nagging shin injury has been reportedly delayed until January. That leaves the misfiring Joshua Zirkzee as the only orthodox striker available for the Red Devils, which is an alarmingly bleak prospect.

Šeško’s 12-goal debut season offered encouragement that United had finally clinched their long-term No. 9 after painful experiences with Zirkzee and Rasmus Højlund. Despite his worrying injury record, the Slovenian sharpshooter remains part of the club’s vision of a brighter future.

But nobody can deny United’s need for reinforcements. The club, as they should have over the summer, will need to sign an alternative to Šeško when the transfer market re-opens in January, preferably recruiting a short-term solution which will bolster their ranks without blocking the development of their injured 23-year-old.
Here are five strikers they could turn to in the winter window.

Jean-Philippe Mateta has long wanted to leave Crystal Palace. / BSR Agency/Getty ImagesPremier League proven and out of contract next summer, Jean-Philippe Mateta could be the perfect answer to United’s prayers.

It’s no secret the 29-year-old has long wanted to leave Crystal Palace, even coming close to joining AC Milan last winter before issues with his medical scuppered a move. He’s begrudgingly continued to represent the Eagles, and he finished last season with 16 goals across all competitions despite his itchy feet—the third successive campaign in which he’s hit double-digits.

Mateta won’t be signing a contract extension at Selhurst Park, meaning the upcoming January window is the last chance Palace have to cash in on him. Given his proposed move to Milan was valued at around $36 million, one would expect United to be able to sign him for even less this winter.

Old Trafford would certainly prove an attractive destination for Mateta, in spite of the Red Devils’ current predicament. The chance to join one of the world’s grandest clubs—one currently playing Champions League soccer—doesn’t arise every day.

The towering center forward would prove similarly appealing for United. Clinical, powerful, cost-effective and acutely aware of the demands of English soccer, Mateta would provide excellent competition for Šeško in both the immediate future and years to come.
Endrick is desperate for more game time. / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIf United desire an incredibly short-term remedy, then Endrick would be worth analyzing closely.

Real Madrid blocked a possible loan exit for their young Brazilian over the summer, but it’s been a familiar story for him at the beginning of the José Mourinho era. The continued brilliance of Kylian Mbappé and arrival of summer recruit Carlos Espí has resulted in a bit-part role, which has yielded just four appearances.

A dramatic increase in game time appears unlikely during the second half of the campaign, potentially forcing Endrick into another temporary departure. He spent half of the 2025–26 season on loan with Lyon in France, where he delivered an impressive eight goals and as many assists in 21 outings.
The raw talent is undeniable, and United could take a fairly risk-free punt on the 20-year-old as a result.

Whether Madrid will actually sanction his exit, either temporarily or permanently, remains to be seen, as does his effectiveness as a sole striker in the Premier League. But Endrick ticks a number of United’s boxes regardless.
Could Alexander Sørloth be a surprise solution? / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesErling Haaland lite, anyone?

Alexander Sørloth resembles his Norwegian compatriot in many departments. The 30-year-old has an imposing frame, excellent aerial ability and a ruthless streak in the penalty area—traits he’s regularly exhibited during his spell in Spain with Real Sociedad, Villarreal and now Atlético Madrid.

He’s registered 20+ goals in each of his past three seasons and finished in La Liga’s top four scorers in two of those campaigns, despite the fact he’s often not been a regular starter since moving to Atlético.
